newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Russia, Czech Republic sign debt deal - PM.
newsitem.headline: Russia, Czech Republic sign debt deal - PM.

text.p: Russia and the Czech Republic signed on Monday an agreement covering interest payments on Russian debt to Prague, Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said after talks with Russian Premier Viktor Chernomyrdin.

"We signed an agreement in 1994 and a supplement was signed today. The supplement deals with the way to deal with interest payments for 1995-7, which will be made partially in cash and partially in goods," Klaus told a joint news conference with Chernomyrdin.
Russia agreed in May 1994 to pay back loans to the former Soviet Union from the Czech Republic of some $3.5 billion.
A schedule was agreed to allow Russia to repay the debt in instalments until 2003 but Moscow suspended payments in 1996.
In January 1997, Czech Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik said he had agreed on a payments schedule under which Russia would pay off $190 million a year, of which $126 million was interest.
Klaus said the deal was signed by Finane Ministry officials.
"I believe it is another step forward," he told the news conference. Further details were not immediately available.
